Summary: 
Join a world-leading School of Computer Science and Engineering and help shape the next generation of cybersecurity professionals through innovative, high-quality teaching in areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, wargaming, and offensive and defensive security.

Job Details
•	Salary, 
o	Lecturer (Level B) – AUD $127,947 to $150,830 per annum + 17% superannuation
o	Senior Lecturer (Level C) – AUD $155,403 to $178,290 per annum + 17% superannuation
•	Full-time
•	2-Year Convertible Tenure Track or continuing appointment
•	Location: Kensington – Sydney, Australia

The Opportunity
Join the School of Computer Science and Engineering in the Faculty of Engineering at UNSW as a Lecturer / Senior Lecturer in an Education Focused role. In this role, you will contribute to excellence in teaching and learning within cybersecurity, while helping to shape the next generation of cybersecurity professionals and computing graduates.

You will contribute to teaching across areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, wargaming, offensive and defensive security, and related cybersecurity disciplines at undergraduate and postgraduate levels. You will play a key role in delivering engaging learning experiences, developing innovative curriculum and teaching approaches, and enhancing student learning outcomes.

With established strengths in cybersecurity, systems, artificial intelligence, and software engineering, UNSW offers an exceptional environment for educators who are passionate about teaching excellence, curriculum innovation, and student success. You will contribute to a collaborative academic community committed to advancing education and preparing students for real-world impact.

This is an opportunity to join a global leader in Computer Science, with cutting-edge facilities, world-class faculty, and an innovative educational environment. With strong industry partnerships and a commitment to educational excellence, UNSW provides excellent opportunities for career development, collaboration, and impact.

About You
You are an engaging and passionate educator with expertise in cybersecurity and a commitment to delivering high-quality teaching and learning experiences. You bring knowledge in areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, wargaming, and offensive and defensive security, along with the ability to contribute to an inclusive and high-performing academic environment.

At Lecturer level (Level B), you will contribute to teaching, curriculum development, and student support across undergraduate and postgraduate courses, while continuing to develop your teaching practice and educational innovation capabilities.

At Senior Lecturer level (Level C), you will demonstrate educational leadership through curriculum innovation, mentoring colleagues, leading teaching initiatives, and contributing to the advancement of teaching excellence across the School and broader UNSW Education Focused community.
You are collaborative, adaptable, and motivated to create meaningful learning experiences while building strong relationships across academia and industry.

About UNSW
UNSW is a world leading institution recognised for its scale, prestige, and impact. With strong industry engagement and partnerships across sectors, UNSW provides a unique environment where academic expertise translates into real world outcomes. The university is home to cutting edge research that drives innovation and societal progress, while its excellence in teaching ensures students are prepared to lead in their fields. For academics, UNSW offers an outstanding platform to flourish — combining world class facilities, collaborative networks, and a culture of innovation that supports both career growth and meaningful contributions to the wider community.

The School of Computer Science and Engineering is one of the largest and most prestigious schools of computing in Australia. It offers undergraduate programmes in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, and Bioinformatics, as well as a number of combined degrees with other disciplines. Our research and teaching staff are world leading and world building as they advance knowledge and learning. For more information on our school, please visit: https://www.unsw.edu.au/engineering/our-schools/computer-science-and-engineering 

Skills & Experience:
Lecturer (Level B)
•	A PhD in a related discipline, and/or relevant work experience.
•	Actively stays up to date with discipline knowledge and professional development.
•	Demonstrated experience in teaching and learning design, development and delivery at undergraduate and/or postgraduate level. 
•	Experience using and/or designing with educational technologies and online delivery methods.
•	Evidence of teaching effectiveness and passion for educational excellence (e.g. relevant discipline-based curriculum design and development at a variety of levels and scales).
•	Demonstrated knowledge of industry or experience in work-integrated learning (desirable).
•	Evidence of highly developed interpersonal and organisational skills.
•	Evidence of ability to support and inspire students from diverse backgrounds and support student equity, diversity and inclusion initiatives.
•	An understanding of and commitment to UNSW’s aims, objectives and values in action, together with relevant policies and guidelines.
•	Knowledge of health and safety responsibilities and commitment to attending relevant health and safety training.

Senior Lecturer (Level C)
•	A PhD in a related discipline, and/or relevant work experience.
•	Actively stays up to date with discipline knowledge and development.
•	Demonstrated experience in teaching and learning design using a range of pedagogical approaches, development and delivery of courses and programs, at undergraduate and/or postgraduate level. 
•	Experience in implementing educational technologies and online delivery methods.
•	Evidence of teaching effectiveness and passion for educational excellence and fostering this in others.
•	Demonstrated experience with industry or work-integrated learning. 
•	Evidence of professional development of teaching practice in self and others with the ability to advance and lead an inclusive culture of excellence in learning and teaching.
•	Demonstrated success in initiating curriculum development and improvement.
•	Evidence of highly developed interpersonal and organisational skills.
•	Evidence of ability to support and inspire students from diverse backgrounds and support student equity diversity and inclusion initiatives.
•	Demonstrated ability to interact with the profession and industry and attract funding for learning and teaching initiatives.
•	An understanding of and commitment to UNSW’s aims, objectives and values in action, together with relevant policies and guidelines.
•	Knowledge of health and safety responsibilities and commitment to attending relevant health and safety training.

Additional details about the specific responsibilities for this position can be found in the position description. This is available via JOBS@UNSW. 

To Apply: 
If you are an educator passionate about delivering high-quality teaching and enhancing the student learning experience, whether as an emerging or experienced academic, this opportunity offers the chance to contribute to innovative teaching practices, curriculum development, and educational excellence within the School. We encourage you to click the “Apply Now” button and submit your CV, cover letter, and responses addressing the Skills and Experience criteria.

If you're excited about this role and think you have what it takes, but your experience doesn't align 100%, we still want to hear from you and would encourage you to apply.

If you have had any interruption in your career, you are encouraged to include a ROPE statement as part of your application. For information on ROPE please check: 
https://www.arc.gov.au/about-arc/program-policies/

- Skilled Light Vehicle Mechanic required
- Full time opportunity
- Join the team at Autoworks Pty Ltd

Autoworks Pty Ltd are a busy, independent mechanical workshop specialising in the servicing, maintenance, diagnostics, and repair of a wide range of light vehicles. The workshop offers varied and challenging work in a practical, fast-paced environment where quality workmanship, teamwork, and customer satisfaction are highly valued. It is well suited to someone who enjoys problem-solving, takes pride in their work, and is committed to delivering high-quality mechanical services.

We are seeking a qualified and experienced Light Vehicle Mechanic with strong skills in diagnostics, fault-finding, servicing, and mechanical repairs.

The ideal candidate will have experience working on a wide range of light vehicles and be confident using diagnostic equipment to identify and resolve faults. They should be reliable, detail-oriented, and able to work independently while maintaining high standards of workmanship and safety. Strong communication skills, a positive attitude, and a commitment to delivering quality service are essential.

Your role will include, but is not limited to:
- Diagnose and identify mechanical, electrical and electronic faults in light vehicles using specialised diagnostic equipment and manufacturer specifications to determine appropriate repair solutions.
- Perform scheduled servicing, logbook maintenance and preventative maintenance on a wide range of passenger, performance, classic and modified vehicles in accordance with manufacturer recommendations.
- Repair or replace worn, damaged or defective mechanical components including engine parts, clutches, gearboxes,
differentials, braking components, suspension assemblies, steering systems, cooling systems and exhaust systems.
- Inspect, dismantle, repair and reassemble engines, transmissions, steering, suspension, braking, cooling and driveline systems, ensuring all components meet manufacturer and workshop quality standards.
- Conduct engine diagnostics, electronic fuel injection (EFI) repairs, engine management system testing and fault rectification using computer-based diagnostic equipment.
- Carry out engine overhauls, engine conversions and other mechanical upgrades for light vehicles, ensuring all work is completed safely and in accordance with engineering and workshop specifications.
- Install and integrate performance components and aftermarket mechanical systems, including turbochargers, suspension upgrades and associated vehicle modifications while maintaining vehicle reliability and safety.
- Test, adjust and inspect repaired or serviced vehicles through workshop testing and road testing to verify performance, drivability and compliance with operational and safety requirements.
- Assist with custom vehicle builds by carrying out mechanical installation, fitting and assembly work in collaboration with fabrication and auto electrical teams.

USVD Consultants Pty Ltd (ACN 666 075 065) ABN: 80 993 362 158 is a recruitment company having office at Bella Vista NSW 2153.

Our client Thinksupreme Pty Ltd (TSPL), ABN: 99 648 206 393 (Business name: Supreme Aluminium Windows) located at: Unit 3 78 Heathcote Rd Moorebank NSW 2170. Proudly Australian owned and operated for over 60 years, they have been Sydney's most trusted supplier of aluminium windows & doors. They manufacture a large range of residential and commercial windows and doors using top of the line materials and cutting-edge production technologies. They specialise in New Builds, Developments, Renovations, Office, Commercial or Industrial Windows & Doors.

Due to their business growth and expansion plans, USVD is now looking to recruit Machinist(s) in their Operations team on a permanent full-time basis.

Role: Machinist
No. of positions: Multiple, minimum 02
Reports to: Operations Supervisor
Location: Unit 3 78 Heathcote Rd MOOREBANK NSW 2170
Annual offered salary: AUD $82,000 - $88,000 base + Super (for a 38-hour work week)

Purpose of the role: We are seeking an experienced Machinist or may be two to join our operations team on a full-time basis. Set up and operate lathes, CNC, Milling, Grinding, Drilling & Turning machines to produce metal components to the specified tolerances, in accordance with technical drawings and safety requirements as per Australian standards.

As a Machinist, your main duties and responsibilities include:
•	Interpret engineering and technical drawings, sketches and specifications (including AS 1100/AS 1102 standards) to determine job requirements, tolerances and machining sequences.
•	Set up and operate lathes to perform turning operations, producing components to specified tolerances using a full range of lathe accessories.
•	Set and adjust computer-controlled (CNC) machines and processes, resolving technical difficulties.
•	Set up and operate milling machines to perform milling operations on components to required tolerances and specifications.
•	Set up and operate grinding machines to perform grinding operations and check finished components for conformance to specification. 
•	Set up and operate general workshop machines (drills, saws, etc.) for basic machining operations in a maintenance or jobbing environment.
•	Carry out mechanical cutting and holing operations using a range of cutting equipment.
•	Perform precision mechanical measurement, selecting and applying appropriate measuring instruments and interpreting results.
•	Perform general engineering measurements using mechanical measuring devices and visual inspection techniques. 
•	Use hand tools and portable/fixed power tools safely and correctly for a variety of general engineering tasks.
•	Use tools and equipment to manually produce components to precise dimensions and finishes on metallic and non-metallic materials.
•	Perform routine calculations, including percentages, ratios, proportions and averages, and interpret simple charts/graphs relevant to machining tasks.
•	Shut down and isolate machines and equipment safely in accordance with relevant Australian Standards and WHS legislation.
•	Carry out manual handling of materials and components in line with Safe Work Australia guidelines.
•	Operate fixed/moveable load-shifting equipment to move and position materials and stock.
•	Order and requisition materials, consumables and tooling as required for production and maintenance tasks.
•	Work safely with industrial chemicals, solvents, coolants and materials used in the machining environment.
•	Plan and prioritise daily work activities in line with established procedures and WHS policies.
•	Organise, record and communicate production, job and maintenance information using workplace systems (including computer-based systems). 
•	Participate in and contribute to environmentally sustainable work practices in the workshop.
•	Work effectively as part of a production/engineering team, contributing to team goals and quality outcomes.
•	Assist in providing on-the-job training and guidance to apprentices, trainees or other production staff.
•	Interpret technical specifications and equipment manuals to inform machining and maintenance decisions.
•	Comply with WHS procedures, quality systems and legislative requirements at all times.

Qualification & Licences:
•	Certificate III in Engineering - Mechanical Trade – Metal Machinist (First class) preferred.
•	At least 5 years of proven work experience in the above job role. 
•	Sound experience as Machinist in Metal fabrication environment. 
•	Well experienced of WHS requirements, particularly in manufacturing and steel fabrication environment. 
•	Ability to interpret technical drawings, manuals, and specifications.
Skills:
•	Strong organizational and time management skills 
•	Excellent attention to detail 
•	Ability to multitask and physically fit
•	Process and results driven 
•	Team player; collaborative 
•	Resilient, patient and adaptable 
•	Enthusiastic, self-motivated 
•	Proactive & hard-working

Additional information:
•	Ability to work outside of normal business hours on occasion when delivering key orders. 
•	Ability to travel interstate, if required.
